samples.summary: agent-iterate-ci.yml's permissions block grants no `checks` scope, but the loop-status.mjs it newly invokes reads the check-runs API for every PR commit — both new CI-arm status updates will bail silently
samples.evidence: `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:24-28` sets `permissions: contents: write / pull-requests: write / issues: write / actions: read` — no `checks:`. The two new steps at `:179` ("Update loop status (CI attempts exhausted)") and `:378` ("Update loop status (CI-fix outcome)") run `node ./scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs`, whose `main()` calls `checkRunsFor(sha)` → `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for every commit (scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:255-263, 331). With a restricted `permissions:` block, unlisted scopes are set to none, so that read 403s, `ghJson` throws, and the whole body build falls into `bail("could not build the status body")` → exit 0, continue-on-error step passes green. Net effect: on the CI arm the sticky comment is never posted or flipped to paged, so a PR whose CI-fix loop paged a human keeps whatever the panel last wrote (e.g. "fix round in progress"). Compare the jobs that DO grant it: agent-review-panel.yml:367 (`checks: write`), :1210 (`checks: read`), :1337 (`checks: read`), :1868 (`checks: write`).
searchedFor: compared with permissions blocks of review-panel/promote/fix/stalled jobs

samples.summary: The sticky-comment upsert has no locking, and two workflows can perform the first update concurrently on a red CI — producing two marker comments, one of which is then never updated again
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:350-353` does read-then-write: `comments.find(isOwnStatusComment)` → PATCH, else POST. On a FAILED CI run both `agent-review-panel.yml`'s review-panel job (its "Update loop status (panel verdict)" step, added at :966ff, runs `if: always() && steps.pr.outputs.number != ''` — the panel job is not gated on CI success, only promote/fix are, see :1203 and :1329) and `agent-iterate-ci.yml`'s new steps fire for the same PR at roughly the same time. The docblock's self-healing argument ("re-derived IN FULL on every update") only holds for the ONE comment that keeps being found.

samples.summary: The CI-arm loop-status calls omit --max-rounds, so every CI-fix update erases the "Fix rounds used: N of M" line the panel/promote/fix updates wrote
samples.evidence: `renderLoopStatus` only emits the budget line when BOTH failedRounds and maxRounds are finite (scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:196-201); `flags["max-rounds"]` defaults to null (:341-343). The panel (agent-review-panel.yml:995-999), promote (:1266), guard (:1430) and fix (:1735) calls all pass `--max-rounds ${{ env.MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS }}`, but the two new iterate-ci calls (agent-iterate-ci.yml:188-190 and :396-397) do not — MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS is not defined in that workflow. The comment therefore flip-flops between showing and hiding the round budget depending on which arm updated it last.

samples.summary: loop-status counts fix rounds against the FULL lens manifest, while review-round-guard counts against `required_checks` (applicable blocking lenses only) — the displayed budget can disagree with the authoritative one
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:246-252` builds lens names from `lenses/lenses.json` (all six ids) and `:331` calls `countFailedReviewRounds(commits, lensCheckNames, { since: rerunAt })`. The guard's number — the one that actually pages — uses `requiredCheckNames`, i.e. the panel's `required_checks` output, which includes only lenses that were BLOCKING **and applicable in that round** (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:845-858; scripts/agent/review-round-guard.mjs:226). A lens excluded from `required_checks` in the current round but carrying a `failure` conclusion on an earlier commit still counts in the comment, so the sticky dashboard can read "2 of 3" while the guard is at 1 — the opposite of what a human reading it is deciding on.
searchedFor: read the required_checks computation in agent-review-panel.yml:838-858

samples.summary: `ready: prView.isDraft === false` mislabels the supported non-draft managed path (`agent:managed` / `@claude loop` human PRs) as "ready for human review" / "🤝 promoted" for the whole loop
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:333` passes `ready: prView.isDraft === false`, and `renderLoopStatus` lets `ready` override the event headline and the table's "Then" cell (:187-192, :224-231). Both agent workflows explicitly support PRs that were never drafts: agent-review-panel.yml:186 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:62-66 treat any PR labelled `agent:managed` as managed. On such a PR the dashboard claims promotion from the first update onward. Note the same `isDraft === false → ready` inference already exists in scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:124, so this may be judged an accepted repo-wide convention rather than a new defect.
searchedFor: read the agent:managed gate in both workflows

samples.summary: `@claude fix` and `@claude rerun` never touch the new sticky comment, so after an on-demand fix or a maintainer hand-back the dashboard keeps asserting "🛑 paged to a human" until some other arm happens to update it
samples.evidence: grep for `loop-status` across `.github/workflows` matches only agent-implement.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml and agent-review-panel.yml. `agent-fix.yml` runs a full fix session (and can push) and `agent-rerun.yml` deletes the paged latch comments and re-runs CI (agent-rerun.yml:131-145) — neither refreshes the projection, so the comment contradicts the label state set by those same workflows until the next panel round writes it. Self-healing recovers eventually, but the window is exactly the moment a human has just intervened and is looking at the PR.

samples.summary: Each loop-status update costs one paginated check-runs request per PR commit, now issued from up to four jobs per round and duplicating the guard's identical fetch inside the same job
samples.evidence: `scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:255-263` + `:325-329` fetch every commit of the PR and then its check runs one commit at a time. `review-round-guard.mjs:162-168` performs the identical per-commit fetch, and the new step at agent-review-panel.yml:1417ff runs loop-status in the SAME fix job seconds later, doubling it; promote, panel, iterate-ci and stalled add more. On a long-lived PR (20+ commits) that is 100+ extra REST calls per round on the shared GITHUB_TOKEN budget — and a secondary-rate-limit 403 hits the guard's unforgeable round count, not just this display surface. Caching the guard's already-fetched commits (or reusing check-run data across the two calls) would avoid it.
searchedFor: counted the new loop-status call sites across the three workflows

verdict.reason: Verified independently. agent-iterate-ci.yml's top-level permissions (:24-28) grant contents/pull-requests/issues write and actions:read, with no `checks` scope, and the only other permissions block in the file is on the `gate` job (:46-47, pull-requests: read). The `iterate` job (:72-87) declares no job-level permissions at all, so it inherits the scope-less-for-checks top-level block. Both new steps run loop-status.mjs with GH_TOKEN: secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN (:186, :382) — not the broader App token used at :349/:406 — and loop-status.mjs:316 calls checkRunsFor() for every PR commit, which hits repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/check-runs (:270-277). That call is inside the try block whose catch bails via process.exit(0) (:347-348, :256-259), and both steps are continue-on-error, so the failure is silent/green. No counterexample exists anywhere in the file or in an included/indirect config: every other loop-status.mjs call site in this repo explicitly grants a checks scope (agent-review-panel.yml:367, :1210, :1337, :1868), which is affirmative evidence the scope is required for this API rather than optional. In-lane for blast-radius: a new call site that does not supply a config precondition the invoked script requires, leaving the CI-arm sticky comment never posted or flipped to paged.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. loop-status.mjs:357-371 is an unlocked read-then-write upsert (find → PATCH by id, else POST), with the comment list read even earlier at :309 before a multi-call body build, widening the window. Two writers exist in workflows that cannot serialise each other: agent-review-panel.yml:992-1012 runs under `if: always() && steps.pr.outputs.number != ''` (not gated on CI conclusion) in a workflow whose concurrency group is agent-review-panel-<repo>-<branch>-active|noop (:115-118), while agent-iterate-ci.yml:182-192 and :378-396 run in a workflow whose group is agent-iterate-<branch> (:82-84); both are triggered by workflow_run on "CI" (panel on `requested`, iterate on `completed` + conclusion failure, :19-22/:40-43), so on a red CI both are live for the same PR. No duplicate reaping exists anywhere for LOOP_STATUS_MARKER — contrast metrics.mjs:1050-1054, which deletes all prior SUMMARY_MARKER comments and thereby self-heals; loop-status has no equivalent, so a second POST is orphaned and frozen forever, contradicting the self-healing claim at loop-status.mjs:9-11. I bounded the impact: nothing reads the comment back to gate (references limited to loop-status.mjs and its test; rounds.mjs:41,71-73 latches on a different marker, so no forged paged latch), so this is not critical — but it is a violated "exactly one sticky comment" invariant with a second entry point reaching the same mutation, and a permanently stale loop dashboard misleads the human it exists to inform. Likelihood is lower than the finding suggests (panel writes ~4 min after iterate's paged write in the median case), but the panel step is always(), so an early panel failure lands in the same window; that is a confidence matter, not a severity one. No refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The quoted CI-arm lines exist, but the "boundary" they allegedly bypass does not. The panel's $RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools staging is documented at agent-review-panel.yml:1465-1475 as a script-AVAILABILITY fix for PRs branched before a script shipped, and it explicitly disclaims the trust framing ("It does NOT make the record trusted"); :1675-1676 repeats the same availability rationale. The CI arm covers that same purpose with `[ -f ... ] || exit 0` guards at agent-iterate-ci.yml:191, :336, :387, so nothing reaches a protected operation around a guard. The iterate job executes branch code with tokens by design and pre-diff (branch checkout :97-101, pnpm install :207, summarize-ci.mjs :226, set-state.mjs with GITHUB_TOKEN :252, metrics.mjs with the App token :167/:408; job comment :75-76), and the documented trust model puts the no-branch-code-with-secrets rule on the review/verdict job only (20260720 todo :113-124). No privilege gain either: the fixer at :254-316 already runs arbitrary Bash with an unscoped App token (:90-95, :261), a superset of the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN grant (:24-28). What remains is a cross-workflow security-hardening consistency preference (the reviewer itself flags the metrics.mjs precedent as pre-existing) — a security/trust-model design judgement this lens explicitly defers, with no changed contract, no broken caller, and no in-workflow guard bypass.
